Why we rewrote our build system

For six years our build ran on a pile of shell scripts that nobody fully understood. Every new hire spent their first week learning which scripts were load-bearing and which were fossils, and every release involved at least one person reading a script aloud.

This post is about what we replaced it with, what we got wrong on the way, and the three properties we now think any build system for a team our size has to have: it is hermetic, it is incremental, and its failures name the input that caused them.

The rewrite took four months. The second part covers the migration itself, which was harder than the rewrite.
